subject.title: Feature: Reason-aware cron guardrails (quota/auth/rate-limit aware backoff + circuit breaker)

question: What default recurring cron guard policy should OpenClaw own for billing, auth, format, rate-limit, and quota failures, and which guard state/config/protocol surfaces should ship with it?
rationale: The remaining work changes compatibility-sensitive cron defaults, persisted state, public protocol/UI visibility, and provider/auth cooldown semantics, which automation cannot choose safely without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve coordinated guard layer
options.body: Define and land one reason-aware recurring cron guard policy with explicit state/protocol/docs/tests and compatibility-safe defaults.

options.title: Split into narrower policies
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella but require separate maintainer decisions for billing, auth, rate-limit, quota, and UI/state visibility before implementation.

options.title: Defer core policy
options.body: Leave current generic recurring backoff in place and only accept narrow opt-in PRs until stronger live evidence or product direction exists.

recommendation.title: Approve coordinated guard layer
recommendation.body: Define and land one reason-aware recurring cron guard policy with explicit state/protocol/docs/tests and compatibility-safe defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete provided the prior keep-open review and has adjacent recurring cron retry history, making them the best available routing owner for the policy choice.
